newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK December PSBR data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK December PSBR data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists reactions to UK public sector borrowing requirement which was 2.1 billion sterling in December, vs expected 1.1 bln.

"It's slightly on the disappointing side. There's still a bit of concern on the spending side and as the budget showed, the government was struggling to constrain spending this year, it was only due to one or two special factors they managed to bring down the total."

"I think with this slightly worse number we're still consistent with (a 96/97 target of) 26.4 billion and looking ahead to 1997/98 I think they can do better than their 19.2 billion forecast. We're looking for something around 18 billion, that's with a stronger consumption forecast.
"Overall I don't think there's too much to worry about at this stage on the funding side. But obviously it's a trend you've got to watch, that spending's not allowed to run away before the election."

"The UK PSBR was disappointingly large but does not make the government's full-year forecast look out of reach. The overshoot versus expectations solely reflected higher interest payments, itself a function of the introduction of strippable gilts. As such, the underlying structural position should not be view as a big negative for the fixed income market."

"Clearly this isn't a helpful figure for the government at about one billion sterling above estimates. But I don't think it blows the government target for this year right out of the water because much more important months are going to be January and March with tax payments in January and departmental spending in March. But I think our suspicions that government budget forecasts are optimistic are certainly confirmed by these figures."
